sentences.text: Estimates suggest the animal grew to be 10 to 12 meters long and weighed between 7 and 10 metric tons.
The species was named Lessemsaurus sauropoides by José Fernando Bonaparte in 1999 to honor the science writer Don Lessem.
This extinct sauropodiform dinosaur lived in the Los Colorados Formation of Argentina during the Norian stage of the Upper Triassic.
Fossils of this animal date to the mid-Norian stage, approximately 213 million years ago.
In 2018, researchers placed the genus in a new family called Lessemsauridae.
A 2020 study by Oliver W. M. Rauhut and colleagues classified the animal outside the group Sauropoda.
The animal was originally thought to belong to the family Melanorosauridae before being grouped into the new family Lessemsauridae.
The fossil record for this genus spans from 227.3 to 205.7 million years ago.
